territorial_scope.description: Applies to persons that conduct business in Montana or that target products or services to Montana residents, which reaches out-of-state actors targeting the state.

evidence.quote: persons that conduct business in this state or persons that produce products or services that are targeted to residents of this state

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Governs controllers and processors above consumer-count thresholds. Grants Montana residents rights to access, correct, delete, port and opt out of personal data processing, and imposes notice, security, assessment and minor-protection duties. The attorney general enforces it through civil penalties.
summary.long: Applies to persons doing business in Montana or targeting its residents that control or process personal data of at least 25,000 consumers, or 15,000 consumers while deriving over 25% of gross revenue from selling personal data. Consumers may access, correct, delete and port personal data and opt out of targeted advertising, sales and certain profiling; controllers must respond within 45 days, extendable by 45, and offer an appeal. Controllers must limit collection, secure data, obtain consent for sensitive data, avoid discrimination for exercising rights and publish a privacy notice; processors act under contract terms. Data protection assessments are required for heightened-risk processing of activities created after January 1, 2025. Controllers offering online services to known minors must use reasonable care, obtain consent before targeted advertising, sale or certain profiling of minors, and assess heightened risks to minors from October 1, 2025. Exemptions include state and local government bodies, certain banks, insurers and HIPAA covered entities, and institutions of higher education. The attorney general has exclusive enforcement authority and may seek civil penalties of up to $7,500 per violation; the Act creates no private right of action.

notes: Registry metadata names SB 384 (2023), but the document cites only Ch. 681, L. 2023 and Ch. 567, L. 2025. The document is an excerpt: sections 30-14-2805 to 30-14-2807 and 30-14-2810 are absent, so references to them cannot be checked. Dates conflict: 30-14-2814(6) applies data protection assessments to processing after January 1, 2025, while 30-14-2819 applies from October 1, 2025 for minors' services; both are coded as stated. 30-14-2809(3)(b) sets a January 1, 2025 deadline for opt-out preference signals. Definitions differ: 30-14-2802(16) defines Minor as under 18, 30-14-2802(5) defines Child as under 13, and 30-14-2812(2)(d) uses ages 13 to under 16. Federal and Montana references are listed, not exhaustively; others in the text (e.g., 42 U.S.C. 290dd-2, 45 CFR part 46, 47 U.S.C. 153(53)) are not coded. The section_status relations entry is a schema placeholder because relations are populated.

thresholds.variable_text: number of consumers whose personal data is controlled or processed
thresholds.measurement: Number of consumers whose personal data the person controls or processes; no measurement window stated. Excludes personal data controlled or processed solely to complete a payment transaction.
thresholds.consequence: Part applies to persons doing business in Montana or targeting Montana residents that meet this count (or the 15,000-consumer and revenue test in 30-14-2803(1)(b)).
thresholds.conditions: Persons conduct business in this state or produce products or services targeted to residents of this state; excludes personal data controlled or processed solely for completing a payment transaction.

evidence.quote: control or process the personal data of not less than 25,000 consumers, excluding personal data controlled or processed solely for the purpose of completing a payment transaction

thresholds.variable_text: number of consumers whose personal data is controlled or processed, combined with gross revenue from sale of personal data
thresholds.measurement: Number of consumers whose personal data the person controls or processes; no measurement window stated.
thresholds.consequence: Part applies to persons meeting this count together with the revenue condition.
thresholds.conditions: Must also derive more than 25% of gross revenue from the sale of personal data.

evidence.quote: control or process the personal data of not less than 15,000 consumers and derive more than 25% of gross revenue from the sale of personal data

thresholds.variable_text: share of gross revenue derived from the sale of personal data
thresholds.value_text: more than 25% of gross revenue from the sale of personal data
thresholds.measurement: Share of gross revenue derived from sale of personal data; measurement window not stated.
thresholds.consequence: Together with the 15,000-consumer count, brings the person within the scope of the part.
thresholds.conditions: Must also control or process the personal data of not less than 15,000 consumers.

evidence.quote: derive more than 25% of gross revenue from the sale of personal data

thresholds.variable_text: radius within which location data identifies an individual's specific location (precise geolocation data)
thresholds.measurement: Accuracy radius of the location information; the text does not state how it is measured.
thresholds.consequence: Location data meeting this precision is precise geolocation data, which is sensitive data under 30-14-2802(28)(d).
thresholds.conditions: Location must directly identify the specific location of an individual with precision and accuracy.

evidence.quote: directly identifies the specific location of an individual with precision and accuracy within a radius of 1,750 feet

thresholds.variable_text: age of an individual defined as a child
thresholds.measurement: Age of the individual; the text does not state how age is determined.
thresholds.consequence: Personal data collected from a known child is sensitive data; parental consent applies to a minor who is a child under 30-14-2811(3)(a)(ii).
thresholds.conditions: Applies to a known child or a minor for purposes of parental consent requirements.

evidence.quote: "Child" means an individual under 13 years of age.

thresholds.variable_text: age of a consumer defined as a minor
thresholds.measurement: Age of the consumer; the text does not state how age is determined. Applies where the controller actually knows or willfully disregards minority.
thresholds.consequence: Duties of controllers toward minors apply, including the duty of care, limits on processing and consent requirements in 30-14-2811.
thresholds.conditions: Controller offers an online service, product or feature to a consumer whom the controller actually knows or willfully disregards is a minor.

evidence.quote: "Minor" means a consumer who is under 18 years of age.

thresholds.variable_text: age of a consumer for which targeted advertising or sale of personal data requires consent
thresholds.value_text: at least 13 years of age but younger than 16 years of age
thresholds.measurement: Age of the consumer; applies where the controller has actual knowledge or willfully disregards the age. Age is not determined by a stated method.
thresholds.consequence: Processing for targeted advertising or selling the consumer's personal data without the consumer's consent is prohibited.
thresholds.conditions: Requires actual knowledge or willful disregard that the consumer is in this age range.

evidence.quote: at least 13 years of age but younger than 16 years of age
